items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage: "Hand me the long net," Shamsuddin said on the first morning the pool's opening was delayed, and I did, because he seemed to know what he was doing. I was Moshe, a visitor with a swim cap and nothing to do in Addis Ababa until the pump was fixed. We skimmed jacaranda petals off the salt water while the attendant argued on the telephone. It was faintly comic: two grown men, strangers, fishing for flowers. By the fourth morning I was arriving early. Shamsuddin had brought a second net, newer, its handle wrapped in blue tape, and he passed it to me without a word, as one passes a cup at a table. I found I did not want the pump repaired. When it hummed back to life on the sixth day, we stood at the edge holding our nets, oddly formal, as though someone ought to make a speech. Swimmers were already lining up at the gate with towels over their shoulders.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
options: From open frustration at a broken pump to triumphant pride when the narrator repairs it himself
From suspicious distance between two strangers to bitter rivalry over who may use the pool
From cheerful excitement about swimming to gloomy boredom during a long and pointless wait
From mild amusement at an odd shared task to a quiet tenderness toward the routine itself
items.explanation: 초반에 화자는 낯선 두 어른이 꽃잎을 건지는 일을 '약간 우스꽝스럽다'고 묘사한다. 나흘째부터는 일찍 오고, 말없이 건네받은 새 그물을 식탁의 잔처럼 여기며 펌프가 고쳐지지 않기를 바라게 된다. 따라서 가벼운 재미에서 그 일상 자체에 대한 조용한 애정으로 바뀐다는 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 펌프를 고치지 않았고, B와 C의 경쟁심이나 지루함은 지문과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Kagiso never hurried at the post office. He stood at the counter with his hat in his hands while the clerk weighed a parcel of seed catalogs, and he answered every question about the rain twice. Marcus, the surveyor from Cape Town, stood behind him checking his watch, a loan document under his arm that needed the farmer's signature before the afternoon bus. At first Marcus tapped the paper against his leg. Then the clerk mentioned that Kagiso's late wife had once run this counter, and that the old scale was hers. Marcus stopped tapping. He looked at the brass weights, worn smooth at the handles, and at the farmer's careful fingers, and he thought of the six-month extension his office liked to call a favor. When Kagiso finally turned around, Marcus found himself asking about the rain. Outside, the bus driver honked once and pulled away down the gravel road.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a man's impatience with a slow errand, then traces how a revealed detail alters his outlook.
It describes a farmer's financial troubles, then explains the legal terms of the loan he is offered.
It recounts a dispute at a post office, then shows how the clerk settles it in the farmer's favor.
It contrasts life in the city with life on a farm, then argues that rural customs are worth preserving.
items.explanation: 지문은 시계를 보며 서류로 다리를 두드리는 Marcus의 조급함으로 시작한다. 이후 저울이 Kagiso의 죽은 아내 것이었다는 사실이 드러나자 Marcus는 두드리기를 멈추고, 대출 연장을 다시 생각하며 결국 자신도 비 이야기를 묻는다. 따라서 조급함을 제시한 뒤 드러난 세부 사실이 시각을 바꾸는 과정을 따라간다는 A가 정답이다. B의 법적 조건 설명, C의 분쟁 해결, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Anselm cooked by ear. On Thursdays he brought his goulash to the weaving cooperative in Vienna where my mother worked, and the women at the looms would stop their shuttles to ask what he put in it. He always shrugged. When my mother died, I asked him to write the recipe down, partly to test him, partly because I did not yet trust a stepfather to keep anything of hers. He tried. He sat at the kitchen table with a pencil for an hour and produced three lines, one of which said only "enough paprika." I, Liesel, was furious, then puzzled. Then, watching him cook the next Thursday, I began to understand. He tasted, waited, added, tasted again, listening to the pot the way the weavers listened to their looms for a slipped thread. Now I bring the goulash myself. The cooperative has new looms, painted green, that clatter louder than the old ones.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It lists the ingredients of a family dish, then explains how each one came to be included.
It describes the weaving process in detail, then compares it unfavorably with home cooking.
It introduces a man's unwritten method, then traces the narrator's shift from distrust to understanding.
It recounts a mother's death, then argues that recipes should always be recorded in writing.
items.explanation: 지문은 귀로 요리하는 Anselm과 늘 어깨만 으쓱하는 그의 방식을 먼저 소개한다. 이어 화자는 의붓아버지를 믿지 못해 레시피를 적어 달라고 했다가 세 줄짜리 메모에 화를 내지만, 요리하는 모습을 보며 베틀 소리를 듣는 직공처럼 냄비에 귀 기울이는 방식을 이해하게 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 재료를 나열하지 않고, B는 직조를 자세히 설명하지 않으며, D는 오히려 적을 수 없는 방식을 이해하는 글이라 맞지 않다.

items.passage: I rode Darnell's bus for nine years before I saw him without his uniform. That was the Sunday my aunt's church on 47th Street lost its kitchen to a fire and borrowed the narrow galley of a retired lake freighter that a neighbor had turned into a diner on the South Side. The congregation always served fried catfish after service; Darnell's mosque, it turned out, held its Sunday lunch on the same block, and the fire had displaced them too. One galley, one long steel table. For an hour the two groups ate in careful halves, salt shakers lined up like a border. Then Darnell, who knew half the room by their bus stops, began passing plates across the line, calling people by where they got off: Cottage Grove, Halsted, King Drive. "Kenya, Ashland Avenue, pass the hot sauce," he told me. By dessert the halves had blurred. I still take his route, though I sit nearer the front now. Through the windows, the lake looks gray most mornings, then suddenly green.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a fire in detail, then explains how the church planned to rebuild its kitchen.
It compares two religious traditions, then argues that one meal should replace the other.
It recounts a bus driver's daily route, then lists the stops where most passengers get off.
It introduces a forced sharing of space, then shows how one person eases the divide between groups.
items.explanation: 지문은 화재로 두 공동체가 하나의 좁은 주방과 식탁을 함께 써야 하는 상황을 먼저 제시하고, 소금통이 국경처럼 늘어선 어색한 분리를 보여 준다. 이후 Darnell이 사람들을 내리는 정류장 이름으로 부르며 접시를 건네자 디저트 무렵 경계가 흐려진다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 화재와 재건 계획을 다루지 않고, B는 한쪽 식사로 대체하자고 주장하지 않으며, C의 정류장 이름은 사람들을 잇는 수단일 뿐 목록이 글의 구조가 아니다.

items.passage: By eleven at night, the metro platform in Gdansk belonged to Jakub and Eitan and whoever was waiting for the last train. They played the song they had written together the winter before, Jakub on guitar, Eitan on clarinet, and when a student asked who wrote it, Jakub said, "I did," before Eitan could open his mouth. Eitan kept playing. __He had written the bridge on the back of a parking ticket, and he could still feel the shape of the paper in his coat pocket.__ The student dropped a coin into the case and thanked Jakub. When the train arrived, Eitan packed his clarinet slowly, while Jakub counted the coins aloud, dividing them into two equal piles as if fairness were a matter of arithmetic. The doors chimed. A pigeon walked the length of the empty platform.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals Eitan's private evidence of his contribution, sharpening the unfairness of Jakub's claim.
It explains why Eitan is careless about money, foreshadowing his loss of the coins later on.
It suggests that Eitan wrote the entire song alone, contradicting the earlier account of the duo.
It describes the cold weather on the platform, establishing the setting before the train arrives.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 직전에 Jakub은 곡을 자기가 썼다고 말하고, 밑줄 문장은 Eitan이 브리지 부분을 주차 딱지 뒷면에 썼고 그 종이를 아직 주머니에 지니고 있음을 보여 준다. 뒤이어 Jakub이 동전을 똑같이 나누며 공정함을 산수로 여기는 장면과 결합해 공로 인정의 불공평함이 더 두드러진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 돈 분실, C의 혼자 작곡, D의 날씨 묘사는 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: I was twelve the summer my grandfather began teaching me Quechua in the boarding-house kitchen in Lima, between the breakfast dishes and the lunch rush. Winifred, who owned the house, let us use the corner table if we peeled potatoes while we talked. My grandfather corrected me with a grunt and my full name, Rosalinda, never with praise, and he pretended to read the newspaper whenever I got a phrase right. One morning, without thinking, I asked Winifred for the salt in his language. __My grandfather turned a page of the newspaper he had already turned twice.__ Winifred, who did not speak a word of it, handed me the salt anyway, laughing. That night I heard him on the telephone with my mother, repeating my sentence to her slowly, as if reading it from a plaque. In the morning the potatoes were waiting, already washed, in a blue enamel bowl.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that the grandfather is bored by the lesson, explaining why he later stops teaching.
It hints at a pride the grandfather conceals, which a later scene confirms more directly.
It reveals that the grandfather cannot read well, contrasting him with the educated landlady.
It marks the moment the narrator gives up the language, leading to her call with her mother.
items.explanation: 앞에서 할아버지는 손녀가 맞게 말할 때마다 신문을 읽는 척한다고 소개되므로, 이미 두 번 넘긴 면을 또 넘기는 밑줄 문장은 감정을 숨기는 행동으로 읽힌다. 그날 밤 그가 엄마에게 손녀의 문장을 명판을 읽듯 천천히 되풀이하는 장면이 그 자부심을 더 직접적으로 확인해 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 수업을 그만두지 않았고, C의 읽기 능력이나 D의 포기는 지문과 맞지 않다.

items.passage: Ephraim refused my invitation the way he refused everything, politely and at length. I had asked him to Christmas dinner, four floors up, and he stood by the dry fountain in our Manchester courtyard explaining that a man who had spent thirty years at sea did not need company to know what day it was. I said fine, Casey could take a hint, and went upstairs. __Later I noticed he had swept the fountain's basin clean of leaves, though no water had run in it for years.__ On Christmas afternoon I left a plate covered in foil on the fountain's edge. When I came down at dusk the plate was gone, and in its place was a small brass knot, the kind sailors tie for practice, set exactly in the center of the basin. A delivery van idled at the gate, its wipers going though the rain had stopped.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Ephraim plans to restore the fountain, which becomes the main subject of the essay.
It explains why the narrator withdraws her invitation, setting up a later quarrel between them.
It suggests a care Ephraim will not voice, anticipating his indirect reply to the narrator's gift.
It describes the courtyard's neglect, establishing that the building's residents rarely meet.
items.explanation: Ephraim은 초대를 정중하지만 길게 거절하지만, 밑줄 문장에서 그는 물도 없는 분수대를 깨끗이 쓸어 둔다. 이는 말로 표현하지 않는 배려를 암시하며, 뒤에서 화자가 둔 접시 대신 분수대 한가운데 놓인 매듭이 그 간접적인 답장이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 분수대 복원 계획, B의 다툼, D의 주민 간 단절은 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Dario wanted a haircut, and I was paid to translate. That was the arrangement in Havana: he was a visiting engineer with a contract to sign at four, and I, Valentina, went wherever his Spanish failed him. The barber, an old man with a radio playing baseball, told us that by custom he cut no hair on the afternoon of a game. I translated it plainly. Dario laughed and offered twice the price. I translated that too, though more slowly. The barber turned the radio up. __I had a rule, learned in my first year, never to soften what either side said.__ So I did not tell Dario that the barber's son had pitched for the city team until his arm gave out, as the man in the next chair had whispered to me. Dario left with his hair uncut. At four, under the conference room's buzzing lights, he signed his contract with the collar of his shirt turned up against the draft.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals the narrator's dislike of Dario, explaining why she sabotages his business meeting.
It introduces a custom of the barbershop, which the barber then explains to his customers.
It summarizes the narrator's training, showing that she regrets becoming an interpreter.
It states a principle the narrator follows, which frames her decision about what to leave out.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 어느 쪽의 말도 누그러뜨리지 않는다는 통역사의 원칙을 밝힌다. 앞에서 화자는 이발사와 Dario의 말을 그대로 옮기고, 뒤에서는 이 원칙 때문에 옆 손님이 속삭인 이발사 아들의 사연을 Dario에게 전하지 않는다. 따라서 원칙이 무엇을 빼고 전할지의 결정을 틀 짓는다는 D가 정답이다. A의 방해, B의 이발소 관습 소개, C의 후회는 밑줄 문장의 기능과 맞지 않다.

items.passage: Who counts the steps of a stairwell after forty years? Katarzyna did, every evening, one hundred and twelve from the street door to her landing in the old building in Naples, and the number had never once changed. Lakshmi, who had inherited the building from her father, met her on the third floor with an envelope. The rent was going up; a hotel group had made an offer for the whole block. Lakshmi had lain awake rehearsing this and still delivered it badly, apologizing in the wrong places. Katarzyna had expected it for a year and had prepared nothing at all, so she listened with her hand on the rail, polished pale by her own palm. Each woman, in her way, was trying to be decent about something neither had chosen. When Katarzyna finally took the envelope, she thanked Lakshmi for bringing it in person, which was more than her father had ever done. Then she climbed the remaining steps, counting aloud.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Lakshmi and Katarzyna?
options: Openly critical of Lakshmi for selling the building and dismissive of Katarzyna's attachment
Amused by both women's habits and doubtful that either understands the offer being made
Admiring of Katarzyna's defiance and contemptuous of Lakshmi's attempts to apologize
Sympathetic toward both, presenting each woman's difficulty without taking a side
items.explanation: 서술자는 밤새 연습하고도 서툴게 사과하는 Lakshmi의 불안과, 1년간 예상했지만 아무 준비도 못 한 Katarzyna의 처지를 나란히 같은 비중으로 그린다. 또 두 사람 모두 원치 않은 일에 품위를 지키려 한다고 서술하고, Katarzyna가 직접 와 준 Lakshmi에게 고마워하는 장면으로 어느 편도 들지 않는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 한쪽을 비난하는 태도이고, B는 두 사람이 상황을 이해하지 못한다는 근거가 없다.

items.passage: A smell of rosin and radiator dust hung in the music room after school, where Mabel waited for her stepdaughter to finish practicing. For four months Harriet had spoken to her only in logistics: rides, money, a form to sign. Mabel had stopped trying clever openings. She sat on a folding chair by the timpani, pretending with the conviction of a bad actor to grade quizzes she had already graded twice. Harriet played the same eight bars of a sonata, missed the same note, and played them again. On the ninth try she stopped. "You can say it's bad," she said, without turning around. Mabel considered several answers, each more careful than the last, and gave none of them. "It's the F," she said. "Your mother used to miss it too." Harriet's bow hovered. Then she played the bars once more and, deliberately, missed the F again. Snow ticked against the tall windows, and the radiator knocked twice like a latecomer.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Mabel?
options: Gently amused by her awkwardness yet sympathetic to her patient effort to reach Harriet
Harshly critical of her dishonesty and convinced that she has damaged the family further
Coolly detached from her feelings and interested mainly in the technical details of music
Openly mocking of her musical ignorance and impatient with her reluctance to speak plainly
items.explanation: 서술자는 이미 두 번 채점한 시험지를 '서툰 배우처럼' 채점하는 척하는 Mabel을 가볍게 놀리듯 묘사한다. 그러나 넉 달간 사무적인 말만 들으면서도 영리한 말 걸기를 그만두고 조심스러운 답 대신 진솔한 한마디를 고르는 모습을 공감 어린 시선으로 따라간다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지나치게 적대적이고, C는 Mabel의 내면을 세밀히 그리는 서술과 맞지 않다.

items.passage: We had planned the surprise for weeks: on the last night shift before the clinic closed for renovation, Yona and Xinyi would carry the old break-room table out to the hillside terrace so the three of us could watch the sun come up over the plateau. Yona borrowed a truck with the gravity she gives a medication count; Xinyi, who never forgets anything, brought a thermos and three folding chairs. Everything worked. The sky went orange on schedule, and a hawk crossed it as though hired. And yet we sat there saying very little. Yona kept checking her phone for messages from the day staff. Xinyi rubbed at a coffee ring on the table, a stain from some forgotten night years before. I do not blame them, or myself. I have come to think a good plan can arrange the scenery but not the feeling, and that the arranging was its own kind of kindness. On the drive down, the truck's radio found a station playing fiddle music, then lost it in the canyon.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Yona and Xinyi?
options: Disappointed in their lack of enthusiasm and regretful about having joined the plan at all
Affectionate and appreciative of their care, even though the outing did not lift their mood
Puzzled by their sudden silence and suspicious that they were hiding news about the clinic
Envious of their friendship and resentful at being left out of the planning for the morning
items.explanation: 화자는 Yona가 약품 수량을 셀 때처럼 진지하게 트럭을 빌리고 Xinyi가 무엇 하나 잊지 않고 의자까지 챙겼다고 애정 어린 시선으로 묘사한다. 계획대로 됐는데도 아무도 기분이 나아지지 않았지만, 화자는 그들을 탓하지 않고 준비한 일 자체가 친절이었다고 말한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 후회, C의 의심, D의 질투는 지문 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Jamal ran the only all-night pharmacy in our corner of the Delta, and for most of my teens I worked the counter beside him from ten until dawn. We had an agreement, never spoken, that we would not talk about my mother's leaving. Instead we talked about insulin prices, cotton futures, the trucker who bought antacid every Tuesday. I used to think this was cowardice, his and mine. I was Devon then, sixteen and certain I knew everything. Now, writing it down, I see how carefully he built those nights: the radio always tuned to the blues station she liked, her old stool kept behind the register though no one sat on it, the coffee made too strong, the way she made it. He was not avoiding her. He was keeping a room for her and letting me stay in it with him. Outside, the crop dusters started at five, low over the fields, their engines like a second dawn.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward his father in the text?
options: Lingering resentment at his father's refusal ever to discuss the mother's departure
Amused indifference toward his father's habits, which he regards as harmless quirks
A revised, tender understanding of silences he once judged as mere avoidance
Sharp disapproval of his father for running a business that kept his son up all night
items.explanation: 화자는 예전에는 어머니 이야기를 피하는 침묵을 비겁함이라 여겼다고 말한다. 그러나 지금은 어머니가 좋아하던 라디오 채널, 비워 둔 의자, 진한 커피를 떠올리며 아버지가 그녀를 위한 자리를 지키고 있었다고 다시 이해한다. 따라서 과거의 판단을 고친 다정한 이해라는 C가 정답이다. A의 원망은 과거의 생각일 뿐이고, B의 무관심과 D의 비난은 지문과 맞지 않다.

items.passage: Wrapping paper crackled under Vesna's fingers as she slid the package across the diner table outside Riga, where the orchestra bus had stopped for soup. Inside was a wool scarf in a vivid mustard yellow, the one color Zofia had told the whole string section she could not bear. The conductor held it up and declared it perfect. She wore it through lunch, through the second half of the drive, and onto the stage that night, where it clashed magnificently with the black of the orchestra. Vesna, the youngest player, watched from the last desk with her face burning, half proud and half mortified. Afterward, in the corridor, Zofia folded the scarf carefully and told the stage manager it had kept her warm all evening. Outside, the bus idled in the snow, coughing gray clouds under the parking lot's single streetlamp.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To portray how a conductor's sustained pretense spares the feelings of a young musician
To recount the stops an orchestra makes while traveling by bus to a concert outside Riga
To explain why the conductor dislikes the color yellow and avoids wearing it on stage
To suggest that honesty between people always matters more than politeness or comfort
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 겨자색은 Zofia가 단원들에게 견딜 수 없다고 말한 색으로 소개된다. 그런데 그녀는 그 목도리를 완벽하다며 점심부터 무대까지 내내 두르고, 공연 뒤에도 따뜻했다고 말하며 막내 단원 Vesna의 마음을 지켜 준다. 따라서 지휘자의 지속적인 연기가 어린 단원의 감정을 보호한다는 A가 정답이다. B는 일화의 일부만 요약했고, C는 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지문과 반대되는 일반적 교훈이다.

items.passage: Ink and machine oil were the first smells I learned in the printing room in Chiang Mai, and the third, after a month, was the steam from Kiet's iron. She rented the back corner from the press owner and sewed there with her only apprentice, Zhiming, between the stacks of temple calendars. In my first week I watched Zhiming hand Kiet every pin before she asked for it. By spring Kiet's eyes had begun to fail, and the roles reversed in small ways neither mentioned: Zhiming threaded the needles now, read the measurements aloud, and left the cutting chalk exactly where Kiet's hand would fall. Kiet still announced each morning's work as if she had planned it. Zhiming still said, "Yes, teacher." The press thundered on beside them, turning out invitations for weddings I would never attend, their gold lettering drying in rows along the windowsill.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how the narrator first came to work in a busy printing room in Chiang Mai
To depict how an apprentice quietly shields her teacher's dignity as their roles reverse
To explain how a printing press produces calendars and wedding invitations for temples
To argue that every skilled craft must eventually be handed down to a younger generation
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 처음에는 Zhiming이 Kiet가 요청하기 전에 핀을 건네는 보조 역할을 한다. 봄이 되어 Kiet의 시력이 약해지자 실제로는 Zhiming이 바늘에 실을 꿰고 치수를 읽어 주지만, Kiet는 여전히 작업을 지시하고 Zhiming은 '네, 선생님'이라고 답하며 겉모습을 유지한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 도입 일화만 요약했고, C는 소재는 같지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Manila Bay's lighthouse station had two keepers' cottages joined by a single wall, and for eleven years I shared it with Wira. We knocked twice each evening to say the lamp was lit. When the bureau assigned Mateo to replace her, I resented him on principle, and for weeks I let his knocks go unanswered. Then one night the generator failed, and Mateo climbed the tower with me, holding the flashlight steady while I reset the breaker. Afterward he asked how Wira used to signal, and I found myself teaching him the double knock. Keeping that small ritual alive, I realized, honored her more than my silence ever had. Below us, the fishing boats rocked in a row, their lanterns swinging like loose buttons on a coat.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how the narrator and Mateo worked together to repair a generator that failed one night
To explain how the bureau organized the routines that keepers followed for lighting the lamp
To show how the narrator comes to see that welcoming a newcomer can preserve an old bond
To suggest that people must eventually let go of the past entirely in order to be happy
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 Wira와의 오랜 의리 때문에 새로 온 Mateo의 노크를 외면하지만, 뒷부분에서는 그에게 Wira의 두 번 노크를 가르치며 그 의식을 이어 가는 것이 오히려 Wira를 기리는 일임을 깨닫는다. 두 곳의 대비를 연결하면 새 이웃을 받아들이는 것이 옛 유대를 지키는 길이 될 수 있다는 C가 요지다. A는 발전기 수리 일화만 요약했고, B는 등대 소재를 쓰지만 서술 목적이 다르다. D는 과거를 완전히 버리라는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈으로, 지문은 오히려 과거를 이어 간다.

items.passage: “Leave the back panel; we only need to replace the shelf,” Okja said, handing over the chisel. In the quiet reading room of the Hokkaido library, Caoimhe pried loose the warped board and found an envelope wedged behind it, addressed in faded ink to someone named only as the Thursday reader. That morning the librarian had mentioned an elderly man who came every Thursday and always ran his hand along this very shelf before sitting down. Caoimhe studied the envelope, then cut a shallow groove into the new board, just deep enough to hold it. Okja raised an eyebrow but said nothing about the extra hour it cost. Outside, snow slid from the roof in a long, soft rush.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Caoimhe most likely cut a groove into the new board?
options: She worries that Okja will scold her for disturbing the back panel he told her to leave alone.
She hopes the extra hour of careful work will impress Okja with her skill as a carpenter.
She wants the envelope to stay where the man who visits on Thursdays might still find it.
She believes the library has a rule requiring any lost papers to be stored inside shelves.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: 봉투가 'Thursday reader'에게 쓰여 있다는 점과, 사서가 말한 매주 목요일 이 선반을 손으로 쓸어 보는 노인이 있다는 점을 연결하면 Caoimhe가 편지를 원래 자리에 남겨 두려 한다는 동기가 드러난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 Okja에 대한 걱정이라는 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, B는 '추가 한 시간'이라는 결과를 동기로 착각한 것이다. D는 지문에 없는 도서관 규칙이라는 외부 원인을 끌어왔다.

## 문항
### lit40-medium-07-025 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 tone_shift
[지문]
"Hand me the long net," Shamsuddin said on the first morning the pool's opening was delayed, and I did, because he seemed to know what he was doing. I was Moshe, a visitor with a swim cap and nothing to do in Addis Ababa until the pump was fixed. We skimmed jacaranda petals off the salt water while the attendant argued on the telephone. It was faintly comic: two grown men, strangers, fishing for flowers. By the fourth morning I was arriving early. Shamsuddin had brought a second net, newer, its handle wrapped in blue tape, and he passed it to me without a word, as one passes a cup at a table. I found I did not want the pump repaired. When it hummed back to life on the sixth day, we stood at the edge holding our nets, oddly formal, as though someone ought to make a speech. Swimmers were already lining up at the gate with towels over their shoulders.

[질문] Which choice best describes the shift in tone in the text?
A) From open frustration at a broken pump to triumphant pride when the narrator repairs it himself
B) From suspicious distance between two strangers to bitter rivalry over who may use the pool
C) From cheerful excitement about swimming to gloomy boredom during a long and pointless wait
D) From mild amusement at an odd shared task to a quiet tenderness toward the routine itself

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
초반에 화자는 낯선 두 어른이 꽃잎을 건지는 일을 '약간 우스꽝스럽다'고 묘사한다. 나흘째부터는 일찍 오고, 말없이 건네받은 새 그물을 식탁의 잔처럼 여기며 펌프가 고쳐지지 않기를 바라게 된다. 따라서 가벼운 재미에서 그 일상 자체에 대한 조용한 애정으로 바뀐다는 D가 정답이다. A는 화자가 펌프를 고치지 않았고, B와 C의 경쟁심이나 지루함은 지문과 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-07-026 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Kagiso never hurried at the post office. He stood at the counter with his hat in his hands while the clerk weighed a parcel of seed catalogs, and he answered every question about the rain twice. Marcus, the surveyor from Cape Town, stood behind him checking his watch, a loan document under his arm that needed the farmer's signature before the afternoon bus. At first Marcus tapped the paper against his leg. Then the clerk mentioned that Kagiso's late wife had once run this counter, and that the old scale was hers. Marcus stopped tapping. He looked at the brass weights, worn smooth at the handles, and at the farmer's careful fingers, and he thought of the six-month extension his office liked to call a favor. When Kagiso finally turned around, Marcus found himself asking about the rain. Outside, the bus driver honked once and pulled away down the gravel road.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It presents a man's impatience with a slow errand, then traces how a revealed detail alters his outlook.
B) It describes a farmer's financial troubles, then explains the legal terms of the loan he is offered.
C) It recounts a dispute at a post office, then shows how the clerk settles it in the farmer's favor.
D) It contrasts life in the city with life on a farm, then argues that rural customs are worth preserving.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
지문은 시계를 보며 서류로 다리를 두드리는 Marcus의 조급함으로 시작한다. 이후 저울이 Kagiso의 죽은 아내 것이었다는 사실이 드러나자 Marcus는 두드리기를 멈추고, 대출 연장을 다시 생각하며 결국 자신도 비 이야기를 묻는다. 따라서 조급함을 제시한 뒤 드러난 세부 사실이 시각을 바꾸는 과정을 따라간다는 A가 정답이다. B의 법적 조건 설명, C의 분쟁 해결, D의 주장은 지문에 없다.
### lit40-medium-07-028 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
Anselm cooked by ear. On Thursdays he brought his goulash to the weaving cooperative in Vienna where my mother worked, and the women at the looms would stop their shuttles to ask what he put in it. He always shrugged. When my mother died, I asked him to write the recipe down, partly to test him, partly because I did not yet trust a stepfather to keep anything of hers. He tried. He sat at the kitchen table with a pencil for an hour and produced three lines, one of which said only "enough paprika." I, Liesel, was furious, then puzzled. Then, watching him cook the next Thursday, I began to understand. He tasted, waited, added, tasted again, listening to the pot the way the weavers listened to their looms for a slipped thread. Now I bring the goulash myself. The cooperative has new looms, painted green, that clatter louder than the old ones.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It lists the ingredients of a family dish, then explains how each one came to be included.
B) It describes the weaving process in detail, then compares it unfavorably with home cooking.
C) It introduces a man's unwritten method, then traces the narrator's shift from distrust to understanding.
D) It recounts a mother's death, then argues that recipes should always be recorded in writing.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
지문은 귀로 요리하는 Anselm과 늘 어깨만 으쓱하는 그의 방식을 먼저 소개한다. 이어 화자는 의붓아버지를 믿지 못해 레시피를 적어 달라고 했다가 세 줄짜리 메모에 화를 내지만, 요리하는 모습을 보며 베틀 소리를 듣는 직공처럼 냄비에 귀 기울이는 방식을 이해하게 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 재료를 나열하지 않고, B는 직조를 자세히 설명하지 않으며, D는 오히려 적을 수 없는 방식을 이해하는 글이라 맞지 않다.
### lit40-medium-07-029 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 text_structure
[지문]
I rode Darnell's bus for nine years before I saw him without his uniform. That was the Sunday my aunt's church on 47th Street lost its kitchen to a fire and borrowed the narrow galley of a retired lake freighter that a neighbor had turned into a diner on the South Side. The congregation always served fried catfish after service; Darnell's mosque, it turned out, held its Sunday lunch on the same block, and the fire had displaced them too. One galley, one long steel table. For an hour the two groups ate in careful halves, salt shakers lined up like a border. Then Darnell, who knew half the room by their bus stops, began passing plates across the line, calling people by where they got off: Cottage Grove, Halsted, King Drive. "Kenya, Ashland Avenue, pass the hot sauce," he told me. By dessert the halves had blurred. I still take his route, though I sit nearer the front now. Through the windows, the lake looks gray most mornings, then suddenly green.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
A) It describes a fire in detail, then explains how the church planned to rebuild its kitchen.
B) It compares two religious traditions, then argues that one meal should replace the other.
C) It recounts a bus driver's daily route, then lists the stops where most passengers get off.
D) It introduces a forced sharing of space, then shows how one person eases the divide between groups.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문은 화재로 두 공동체가 하나의 좁은 주방과 식탁을 함께 써야 하는 상황을 먼저 제시하고, 소금통이 국경처럼 늘어선 어색한 분리를 보여 준다. 이후 Darnell이 사람들을 내리는 정류장 이름으로 부르며 접시를 건네자 디저트 무렵 경계가 흐려진다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 화재와 재건 계획을 다루지 않고, B는 한쪽 식사로 대체하자고 주장하지 않으며, C의 정류장 이름은 사람들을 잇는 수단일 뿐 목록이 글의 구조가 아니다.
### lit40-medium-07-030 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
By eleven at night, the metro platform in Gdansk belonged to Jakub and Eitan and whoever was waiting for the last train. They played the song they had written together the winter before, Jakub on guitar, Eitan on clarinet, and when a student asked who wrote it, Jakub said, "I did," before Eitan could open his mouth. Eitan kept playing. __He had written the bridge on the back of a parking ticket, and he could still feel the shape of the paper in his coat pocket.__ The student dropped a coin into the case and thanked Jakub. When the train arrived, Eitan packed his clarinet slowly, while Jakub counted the coins aloud, dividing them into two equal piles as if fairness were a matter of arithmetic. The doors chimed. A pigeon walked the length of the empty platform.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It reveals Eitan's private evidence of his contribution, sharpening the unfairness of Jakub's claim.
B) It explains why Eitan is careless about money, foreshadowing his loss of the coins later on.
C) It suggests that Eitan wrote the entire song alone, contradicting the earlier account of the duo.
D) It describes the cold weather on the platform, establishing the setting before the train arrives.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
밑줄 문장 직전에 Jakub은 곡을 자기가 썼다고 말하고, 밑줄 문장은 Eitan이 브리지 부분을 주차 딱지 뒷면에 썼고 그 종이를 아직 주머니에 지니고 있음을 보여 준다. 뒤이어 Jakub이 동전을 똑같이 나누며 공정함을 산수로 여기는 장면과 결합해 공로 인정의 불공평함이 더 두드러진다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 돈 분실, C의 혼자 작곡, D의 날씨 묘사는 지문 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-07-031 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
I was twelve the summer my grandfather began teaching me Quechua in the boarding-house kitchen in Lima, between the breakfast dishes and the lunch rush. Winifred, who owned the house, let us use the corner table if we peeled potatoes while we talked. My grandfather corrected me with a grunt and my full name, Rosalinda, never with praise, and he pretended to read the newspaper whenever I got a phrase right. One morning, without thinking, I asked Winifred for the salt in his language. __My grandfather turned a page of the newspaper he had already turned twice.__ Winifred, who did not speak a word of it, handed me the salt anyway, laughing. That night I heard him on the telephone with my mother, repeating my sentence to her slowly, as if reading it from a plaque. In the morning the potatoes were waiting, already washed, in a blue enamel bowl.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It shows that the grandfather is bored by the lesson, explaining why he later stops teaching.
B) It hints at a pride the grandfather conceals, which a later scene confirms more directly.
C) It reveals that the grandfather cannot read well, contrasting him with the educated landlady.
D) It marks the moment the narrator gives up the language, leading to her call with her mother.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
앞에서 할아버지는 손녀가 맞게 말할 때마다 신문을 읽는 척한다고 소개되므로, 이미 두 번 넘긴 면을 또 넘기는 밑줄 문장은 감정을 숨기는 행동으로 읽힌다. 그날 밤 그가 엄마에게 손녀의 문장을 명판을 읽듯 천천히 되풀이하는 장면이 그 자부심을 더 직접적으로 확인해 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 수업을 그만두지 않았고, C의 읽기 능력이나 D의 포기는 지문과 맞지 않다.
### lit40-medium-07-032 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
Ephraim refused my invitation the way he refused everything, politely and at length. I had asked him to Christmas dinner, four floors up, and he stood by the dry fountain in our Manchester courtyard explaining that a man who had spent thirty years at sea did not need company to know what day it was. I said fine, Casey could take a hint, and went upstairs. __Later I noticed he had swept the fountain's basin clean of leaves, though no water had run in it for years.__ On Christmas afternoon I left a plate covered in foil on the fountain's edge. When I came down at dusk the plate was gone, and in its place was a small brass knot, the kind sailors tie for practice, set exactly in the center of the basin. A delivery van idled at the gate, its wipers going though the rain had stopped.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It shows that Ephraim plans to restore the fountain, which becomes the main subject of the essay.
B) It explains why the narrator withdraws her invitation, setting up a later quarrel between them.
C) It suggests a care Ephraim will not voice, anticipating his indirect reply to the narrator's gift.
D) It describes the courtyard's neglect, establishing that the building's residents rarely meet.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Ephraim은 초대를 정중하지만 길게 거절하지만, 밑줄 문장에서 그는 물도 없는 분수대를 깨끗이 쓸어 둔다. 이는 말로 표현하지 않는 배려를 암시하며, 뒤에서 화자가 둔 접시 대신 분수대 한가운데 놓인 매듭이 그 간접적인 답장이 된다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 분수대 복원 계획, B의 다툼, D의 주민 간 단절은 지문에 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-07-033 — skill text_structure_purpose · 유형 underlined_portion_function
[지문]
Dario wanted a haircut, and I was paid to translate. That was the arrangement in Havana: he was a visiting engineer with a contract to sign at four, and I, Valentina, went wherever his Spanish failed him. The barber, an old man with a radio playing baseball, told us that by custom he cut no hair on the afternoon of a game. I translated it plainly. Dario laughed and offered twice the price. I translated that too, though more slowly. The barber turned the radio up. __I had a rule, learned in my first year, never to soften what either side said.__ So I did not tell Dario that the barber's son had pitched for the city team until his arm gave out, as the man in the next chair had whispered to me. Dario left with his hair uncut. At four, under the conference room's buzzing lights, he signed his contract with the collar of his shirt turned up against the draft.

[질문] Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
A) It reveals the narrator's dislike of Dario, explaining why she sabotages his business meeting.
B) It introduces a custom of the barbershop, which the barber then explains to his customers.
C) It summarizes the narrator's training, showing that she regrets becoming an interpreter.

[표시된 정답] D

밑줄 문장은 어느 쪽의 말도 누그러뜨리지 않는다는 통역사의 원칙을 밝힌다. 앞에서 화자는 이발사와 Dario의 말을 그대로 옮기고, 뒤에서는 이 원칙 때문에 옆 손님이 속삭인 이발사 아들의 사연을 Dario에게 전하지 않는다. 따라서 원칙이 무엇을 빼고 전할지의 결정을 틀 짓는다는 D가 정답이다. A의 방해, B의 이발소 관습 소개, C의 후회는 밑줄 문장의 기능과 맞지 않다.
### lit40-medium-07-034 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

A) Openly critical of Lakshmi for selling the building and dismissive of Katarzyna's attachment
B) Amused by both women's habits and doubtful that either understands the offer being made
C) Admiring of Katarzyna's defiance and contemptuous of Lakshmi's attempts to apologize

서술자는 밤새 연습하고도 서툴게 사과하는 Lakshmi의 불안과, 1년간 예상했지만 아무 준비도 못 한 Katarzyna의 처지를 나란히 같은 비중으로 그린다. 또 두 사람 모두 원치 않은 일에 품위를 지키려 한다고 서술하고, Katarzyna가 직접 와 준 Lakshmi에게 고마워하는 장면으로 어느 편도 들지 않는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A와 C는 한쪽을 비난하는 태도이고, B는 두 사람이 상황을 이해하지 못한다는 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-07-035 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]

Harriet played the same eight bars of a sonata, missed the same note, and played them again. On the ninth try she stopped. "You can say it's bad," she said, without turning around. [질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Mabel?
A) Gently amused by her awkwardness yet sympathetic to her patient effort to reach Harriet

[표시된 정답] A

서술자는 이미 두 번 채점한 시험지를 '서툰 배우처럼' 채점하는 척하는 Mabel을 가볍게 놀리듯 묘사한다. 그러나 넉 달간 사무적인 말만 들으면서도 영리한 말 걸기를 그만두고 조심스러운 답 대신 진솔한 한마디를 고르는 모습을 공감 어린 시선으로 따라간다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지나치게 적대적이고, C는 Mabel의 내면을 세밀히 그리는 서술과 맞지 않다.
### lit40-medium-07-036 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude

### lit40-medium-07-037 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude

### lit40-medium-07-040 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose

### lit40-medium-07-041 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

### lit40-medium-07-042 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
